title: Dependency injection and inversion of control

videos.script: A class that needs a notifier has two choices. It can build one, or it can be handed one. This lesson is about the second choice, and about who does the handing. {{title}} It starts with a small framework for a loan desk. You write two functions, and the framework decides when they run. That shape has a name, inversion of control. {{desk}} Then the same idea applied to objects. A job that sends notices for overdue loans stops building its own clock and its own notifier. It asks for them in its constructor instead. {{constructor}} Somebody still has to build them. That place is the composition root, one file that wires the whole program. {{root}} Next, a container in thirty lines, so the tools that do this for you stop looking like magic. {{container}} And its evil twin, the service locator, which looks like injection and hides every dependency it touches. {{locator}} The lesson ends where injection pays for itself. A test hands the job a fixed day and a notifier that only takes notes. No mail server, no calendar, no patching. {{test}}
